Retelling: In the month Nisan, in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king, wine was before him, and Nehemiah took up the wine and gave it unto the king. Now Nehemiah had not been beforetime sad in the king's presence. The king said, Why is thy countenance sad, seeing thou art not sick? This is nothing else but sorrow of heart. Then Nehemiah was very sore afraid, and said unto the king, Let the king live for ever: why should not my countenance be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers' sepulchres, lieth waste, and the gates thereof are consumed with fire? Then the king said, For what dost thou make request? So Nehemiah prayed to the God of heaven, and said unto the king, If it please the king, and if thy servant have found favour in thy sight, that thou wouldest send me unto Judah, unto the city of my fathers' sepulchres, that I may build it. And the king said, with the queen also sitting by him, For how long shall thy journey be, and when wilt thou return? So it pleased the king to send him, and Nehemiah set him a time. Moreover he asked for letters unto the governors beyond the river, that they might convey him over till he came into Judah, and a letter unto Asaph the keeper of the king's forest, that he might give him timber to make beams for the gates of the palace which appertained to the house, and for the wall of the city, and for the house that he should enter into. And the king granted him, according to the good hand of his God upon him. When Nehemiah came to the governors beyond the river and gave them the king's letters, Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, heard of it, and it grieved them exceedingly that there was come a man to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.
Discussion: A cupbearer's sad face became a request to rebuild a ruined city — prayed in a breath, answered by a king. Reflect: 1) Why did Nehemiah pray before answering a king who could kill him for sadness? 2) What does it mean to ask for letters and timber, not just permission — practical faith? 3) How do you know when sorrow of heart is a call to act, not just to feel?
Significance: One prayed sentence before a king turned a cupbearer's grief into royal letters and timber: God opens the way for the rebuilding before a single stone is laid.
KeyPeople: Nehemiah; Artaxerxes; Sanballat; Tobiah the Ammonite
